name: LA-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Clay Higgins running with large financial edge
Democrats fragmented across three minimally funded candidates
model.rationale: Higgins holds a seat leaning Republican by 18 points, has out-raised the leading Democrat by more than 35-to-1, and faces a split Democratic field with no outside spending against him. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy incumbent win.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or unified consolidation behind one challenger would be the main thing to watch, though neither appears likely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southwest Louisiana's third district is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, and Clay Higgins is seeking another term as its incumbent. He has built a substantial financial advantage, with roughly $595,000 on hand, while the leading Democratic challenger, John Day, has raised only about $23,000. No outside groups are spending in the race, and no expert ratings or public polls are available.

The Democratic side is divided among three candidates with minimal resources, making consolidation unlikely. Prediction markets give Higgins about a 95 percent chance of winning, consistent with the district's strong partisan lean and the incumbent's advantages. The race is rated Safe Republican with high confidence.
